headline: Rebound broadens into earnings gauntlet, AI capex doubts persist
body: Tuesday's session extended last week's bounce rather than reversing it: the Dow added roughly 1% to close near 52,496, the S&P 500 edged up about 0.3% to 7,712.57, and the Nasdaq Composite was essentially flat, with small caps doing the real work as the Russell 2000 outpaced the mega-cap indices. That's a shift in character from the prior week's rout, when AI-infrastructure spending worries knocked the Nasdaq down roughly 4.5% and the S&P almost 2%, with the selling concentrated in chips and hyperscalers rather than spread evenly across the market. Crude stayed firm near $99 a barrel, keeping an energy-cost undercurrent in the macro picture even as equities recovered. GM and Netflix reported Tuesday, and attention now turns to Tesla, Meta, and IBM, all due after today's close, as the next test of whether the bounce has real legs.

The tone reads as a cautious, earnings-driven reset more than a conviction rally: breadth improving via small caps and value-tilted names suggests some rotation away from the narrow AI-capex trade that dominated recent weeks, but tech itself is still effectively in a 'show me the returns' posture after names like Alphabet drew scrutiny over ballooning capital spending and thinning free cash flow. Today's search results turned up little in the way of concrete retail or social-media positioning, so this read leans on price action, sector leadership, and the earnings calendar rather than any clear crowd signal. Meta's and Tesla's numbers after the bell are the swing factor — a clean beat-and-raise on AI monetization would reinforce the stabilization, while another spending-without-payoff narrative could reopen last week's skepticism toward growth names.
